mechanism_evidence.contract: The internal missing singleton survives copy/deepcopy/pickle as itself: copy.copy(missing) is missing, copy.deepcopy(missing) is missing, and pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(missing)) is missing; captured at the copy.copy/copy.deepcopy/pickle call timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Copy, deepcopy and pickle jinja2.utils.missing at every pickle protocol.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: missing is an instance of a dynamically created type with no __reduce__; copy/deepcopy produce a distinct object and pickle fails or rebuilds a non-identical object, breaking is/is-not comparisons against the singleton.

discriminating_observation.description:
import copy, pickle
from jinja2.utils import missing
c = copy.copy(missing)
print("copy_identity", c is missing)
assert c is missing
d = copy.deepcopy(missing)
assert d is missing
u = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(missing))
print("pickle_identity", u is missing)
assert u is missing
print("f2_missing_singleton", True)

triple.is_identity: copy.copy(missing) is missing; deepcopy is missing; pickle roundtrip is missing (is not a distinct rebuild)
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: singleton semantics globally visible: every holder of the missing reference observes the identical object across copy boundaries

mechanism_evidence.contract: Filters/tests decorated with @async_variant pickle by reference to the identical function object: pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(do_first)) is jinja2.filters.do_first; captured at the pickle call timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Pickle an async_variant-decorated filter such as jinja2.filters.do_first.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: The decorator puts the wrong __name__/__qualname__ on the wrapper, so pickle cannot resolve it ("not the same object as ...") and raises PicklingError.
mechanism_evidence.causal_change: @wraps with split assigned attrs: name/module/qualname from the async function, doc/annotations from the sync function.

discriminating_observation.description:
import pickle
import jinja2.filters
f = jinja2.filters.do_first
u = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(f))
print("pickle_identity", u is f)
assert u is f
assert u is jinja2.filters.do_first
f._f2_probe = 1
assert u._f2_probe == 1
del f._f2_probe
print("f2_pickle_by_reference", True)

triple.is_identity: unpickled filter is the module-level function object (pickle-by-reference identity)
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: attribute set on the original is visible via the unpickled reference (same object, shared by design)
